messages:
maria: quick follow-up to the attention-layout RFC — i think we need a lightweight adapter layer between the opspec and kernel selector so we can support per-model layout without exploding kernel variants. thoughts?
kevin: agree. we hit 20% perf regression on some models when forcing contiguous QKV for kernels tuned for interleaved layouts. adapter could do small reshapes + pointer math.
alex: +1. how are we thinking about the public ABI here? we can't force customers to change model export format. adapter must be internal and transparent.
maria: exactly. internal-only. goal: runtime picks one of: 1) run-native (no copy), 2) fast-reshape (small contiguous temp), 3) kernel-side gather (stride-aware). choose by profile.
dave: concerned about memory pressure on the fast-reshape path. on A100 80GB it's fine, on v4p with 32GB not so much. we need per-device heuristics and an OOM-safe fallback to kernel-side gather.
kevin: perf numbers from yesterday:
```
model A (512 seq, 16 heads):
- interleaved native kernel: 1.0x
- contiguous reshape then kernel: 0.86x
- kernel-side gather (stride): 0.92x
```
So reshape is fastest usually but not always worth peak mem.
alex: what about exposing a per-run override in the config? e.g., "layout_hint": "prefer_native|prefer_speed|prefer_memory" so infra teams can opt in.
maria: yes we should. default=auto. auto uses cost model: mem delta + kernel_perf_estimate + latency SLO.
dave: also we need to think about KV cache layout for streaming decode. switching layouts mid-stream will blow cache continuity. adapter must preserve cache-friendly shapes or provide migration plan.
kevin: good call. for streaming we should prefer stride-aware kernels that accept non-contiguous KV views, avoid copies at all costs.
devex-bot: heads-up: if we change runtime semantics we'll need SDK bumps for tensor packing helpers; i'll draft a changelog and migration guide. :memo:
maria: sketch of the adapter signature i'd propose:
```
// chosen by runtime per request
struct LayoutAdapter { 
  enum Mode {NATIVE, RESHAPE_TEMP, STRIDE_GATHER};
  Mode mode;
  // if RESHAPE_TEMP: allocate temp buffer of bytes size_t
  size_t temp_bytes;
  // kernel-facing metadata: per-tensor stride info, pointers
  const void* q_ptr; const void* k_ptr; const void* v_ptr;
  int head_dim; int num_heads;
};
```
This stays internal; kernel selector returns Mode + metadata.
kevin: selector should also return an estimated token throughput delta so caller can reason about batching tradeoffs.
maria: yes, and a flag if adapter requires contiguous KV for cache (so scheduler won't mix streaming requests across that pin).
dave: operational concerns: rollout plan? i'd prefer canary on Dedicated, then smoke on Hosted with low concurrency. if we hit high OOMs flip to STRIDE_GATHER center-wide.
sre-bot: noted. plan outline: canary 5% dedicated -> monitor OOMs, p99 latency, GPU mem util -> rollback threshold: >1% OOM increase or p99 +20% for 10m.
alex: implementation-wise: 3 work items: 1) kernel selector + cost model, 2) adapter code + minimal alloc arena, 3) scheduler annotations for cache pinning. any volunteers?
kevin: i'll take selector + perf numbers (need small harness).
dave: i'll own scheduler changes and rollout automation.
maria: i'll implement adapter core and tests. devex-bot will draft SDK/migration.
kevin: one more thing: quantized kernels (4/4/8-bit) behave differently with stride math. we need kernel-side tests for quantization pack order.
maria: ack — add quantization dimension to cost model.
kevin: also add small microbenchmarks: head_count, head_dim, seq_len sweep. put harness in eng-runtime/perf.
dave: FYI: keep the legacy planar packing support in the ABI for at least two releases. won't break customers.
alex: sounds good. can we capture this as follow-up RFC? short doc with selector contract, adapter struct, and rollout plan. i'll create a draft and ping reviewers.
maria: thanks folks. i'll post an initial patchset tomorrow. :rocket:
